newsitem.title: USA: Heifer injures nine children at Texas rodeo.
newsitem.headline: Heifer injures nine children at Texas rodeo.

text.p: A rampaging heifer ran through a group of elementary school children on a field trip Friday, injuring nine of them, rodeo officials said.
The heifer broke loose while its young handler was leading it out of a trailer at the Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo.

"We were standing right there by the trailer and it (the heifer) jumped up and started bucking and the kid (leading it out) let it go. It ran over ... and started kicking kids and going crazy," said eyewitness Matt Rendon.

Rocio Janson, a teacher who was leading the field trip, said the children were sitting on the ground outside the Astrodome, where the two-week-long rodeo is held each year, when the loose animal suddenly stormed through them.
"The bull came toward us. He passed through my legs, I don't how, then went through the children and trampled over them," she said.
The children and one adult who suffered shock were taken to a local hospital where a spokesman said they were in good condition. Most of the children suffered only cuts and bruises.
The heifer was eventually captured and penned up, rodeo officials said.
A heifer is actually a young cow that has not yet had her first calf.
